newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - AMR seen as victor in Shuttle bid.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - AMR seen as victor in Shuttle bid.

text.p: AMR Corp is seen as the likely victor in its bid to buy the US Airways Shuttle, a commuter air service now operated by US Airways Group Inc a Citicorp report said.

-- US Airways operates the shuttle under a management contract and holds 47 percent of the equity. AMR Corp's American Airlines made a bid to buy the Shuttle. American's bid, however, is contingent on US Airways' decision not to exercise its option to purchase the Shuttle or its right to match American's offer.
-- US Airways said it is still working with the banks that partially own the Shuttle to determine how it will proceed.

-- "If AMR were to acquire the Shuttle at the proposed price, as we think it is the most likely outcome, we would view such a transaction positively for the company in spite of potentially higher labor costs," Citicorp vice president of investment grade research Ettore Bianchi said in a research report.
-- Bianchi said the potential acquisition of the Shuttle would give AMR the chance to increase its penetration of the eastern United States business traveler market.
-- Bianchi said American would face lower servicing costs than US Airways for the Shuttle's fleet of Boeing Co 727 aircraft because American already has Boeing 727s in its fleet.
-- Bianchi said since US Airways has not yet been able to reach a cost-cutting pact with its unions, the airline would not have the competitive cost structure to operate the Shuttle profitably.
-- Bianchi said US Airways' sale of the Shuttle could be used as an additional "reminder" to the unions about the company's willingness to shrink operations further.
-- Bianchi said that at AMR's proposed $300 million offer to buy the Shuttle, US Airways would net close to $80 million for its stake.
